wrong_claims.quote: The ranking aggregates performance across reasoning, coding, science and language benchmarks.
wrong_claims.correct_value: The ranking cited is the Arena (LMArena) Elo leaderboard as of March 2026: Anthropic 1,503, xAI 1,495, Google 1,494, OpenAI 1,481. It is not an aggregate across benchmark categories.

wrong_claims.quote: AI tools reached 500 million regular users faster than the personal computer, the internet, or the smartphone
wrong_claims.correct_value: The report says generative AI reached 53% population adoption within three years, faster than the PC or the internet. No 500 million figure and no smartphone comparison appear in the report summary.

wrong_claims.quote: Investment in AI infrastructure reached $420 billion globally in 2025 — more than double the 2023 figure.
wrong_claims.correct_value: Not in the report summary. The report gives U.S. private AI investment of $285.9 billion in 2025, 23x China's $12.4 billion.

wrong_claims.quote: 67% of knowledge workers report using AI tools at least weekly. AI-assisted code now accounts for an estimated 35% of all new code committed to public repositories.
wrong_claims.correct_value: Neither figure appears in the report's top takeaways. Its adoption figures are 88% organizational adoption and four in five university students using generative AI.

'For the first time' could not be verified. The 'Key statistics' paragraph looks invented and should be replaced with real report figures.

wrong_claims.quote: The company completed a restructuring in early 2026 that converted it to a more conventional public benefit corporation
wrong_claims.correct_value: OpenAI adopted the PBC structure (OpenAI Group PBC) on October 28, 2025, not in early 2026.

The article is dated April 13 and credits Bloomberg; the original reporting was The Information. wrong_claims.quote: On standard evaluations including MMLU, HumanEval and MATH, GLM-5.1 matches or exceeds GPT-4-class performance across most categories... scoring above 85% on competitive programming benchmarks.

wrong_claims.quote: GPT-5.5 ships with Codex, a dedicated agentic coding layer
wrong_claims.correct_value: Codex is OpenAI's existing coding agent product, which predates GPT-5.5. GPT-5.5 was made available inside Codex; it did not ship Codex.

wrong_claims.quote: The model rolled out to ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Business and Enterprise users on April 24, and is accessible via the OpenAI API.
wrong_claims.correct_value: ChatGPT rollout was April 23, 2026. API access followed on April 24.

wrong_claims.correct_value: Announced April 28, 2026 (after the article date) in limited preview, not general availability.

wrong_claims.quote: Anthropic has built a new model internally codenamed Mythos
wrong_claims.correct_value: It is the public product name 'Claude Mythos Preview', announced April 7, 2026 with Project Glasswing. About 11 launch partners plus 40+ organizations got access.

wrong_claims.quote: Within days, Microsoft, Google, and xAI agreed to give the US government early access to unreleased models for security evaluation through NIST
wrong_claims.correct_value: The agreements were with Commerce's Center for AI Standards and Innovation (CAISI, housed in NIST) and announced May 5, 2026. That is after this article's April 30 date, so 'within days' is anachronistic.

notes: Core facts are real: a restricted cyber-capable model, limited to vetted organizations, and no general release planned. The 'far ahead' quote attributed to Anthropic was not found verbatim. Anthropic's wording is that the model can 'surpass all but the most skilled humans' at finding and exploiting vulnerabilities. The line calling Mythos 'the first publicly acknowledged case of a major AI lab deliberately withholding a model' is doubtful: OpenAI's staged GPT-2 release in 2019 is an earlier case. No source was fetched for it, so it is left in notes, not in wrong_claims.

wrong_claims.quote: Database Sync adds two-way, bidirectional connections between Notion databases and external data sources... changes made in Notion are now reflected in the external system and vice versa
wrong_claims.correct_value: Database sync (beta) is one-way: Workers pull data from any API into Notion databases (e.g., Zendesk tickets, Salesforce data). Write-back is not described.

wrong_claims.quote: Plan Mode is a new AI agent capability
wrong_claims.correct_value: The 3.5 release notes have no 'Plan Mode'. The agent features shipped were the External Agents API (alpha), custom agent tools as Workers (beta), and the Notion Agent SDK (alpha).

wrong_claims.quote: Workers runtime allows developers to write and deploy custom serverless JavaScript functions
wrong_claims.correct_value: Workers are Notion's hosted runtime for custom code, deployed via the new Notion CLI and run in a sandbox. They are free in beta, with pricing on Notion credits from August 11, 2026. 'JavaScript' is not specified in the release notes summary.

notes: The release is real: '3.5: Notion Developer Platform', May 13, 2026. Workers and two-way webhooks (any app can trigger Notion) are confirmed. 'Plan Mode' appears to be invented, and the Database Sync description is wrong.

wrong_claims.quote: Pika released Pika 2.5 alongside PikaStream 1.0
wrong_claims.correct_value: PikaStream 1.0 was announced on its own on April 2, 2026 ('Introducing Real-Time Video Chat for Agents') and does not mention Pika 2.5. Pika 2.5 is a separate, earlier video model. The Pika blog has no joint release and no May 2026 post on this.

wrong_claims.correct_value: Pika's blog has no 'flicker-free' claim.

wrong_claims.quote: PikaStream represents the first production-level implementation of real-time AI video conversation at consumer scale
wrong_claims.correct_value: Unsupported marketing claim; no source.

notes: Both products exist, but the article's framing (a joint May 10 release, flicker elimination, a social video platform) has no primary source. Recommend a rewrite around PikaStream 1.0 (April 2, 2026).
